messages:
Ruth (support): heads-up — multiple customers reporting large number of 5xx responses from the hosted inference endpoint when requests exceed quota. Ticket IDs: #C-9234, #C-9240. They expect 429 but are getting 500/503. Happened ~2024-10-20T14:05Z, spike for ~15m. Sample customer log attached:

Ruth (support): ```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"quota service error", "code":500}
```

Ruth (support): quoting customer's edge logs: "quota-service returned error status from classifier: upstream timeout, mapped to 500". They saw this across regions, mostly us-west-2.

Amit (oncall): investigating now. Can you paste the header the gateway received for those requests? We need to know if rate-limit headers were present. Also @Claire FYI, bad classifier mapping could be from edge change.

Ruth (support): pasted headers from customer trace (redacted):

Ruth (support): ```
x-request-id: rq_01F...
x-quota-key: customer_567
x-quota-usage: 1200
x-quota-limit: 1000
x-gateway-route: /v1/generate
```

Claire (sre): seeing correlated alert in rateguard: quota-classifier latency spike at 14:03Z, many classifier calls timed out to quota-orch (tcp timeout ~3s). Our classifier sidecar sometimes returns 504 and gateway translates to 500. Looks like a route misclassification where timeout path is treated as 5xx rather than a 429/4xx fallback.

Evan (runtime): adding logs from edge (filtered):
```
[14:03:12] classifier_request id=rq_01F path=/v1/generate -> call quota-orch (10.20.5.4:8080)
[14:03:15] classifier_response id=rq_01F status=timeout (no response)
[14:03:15] edge_mapper id=rq_01F mapped_status=500 reason=classifier-timeout
```

Evan (runtime): reproducer (local):
```bash
# simulate slow quota-orch so classifier times out
kubectl port-forward svc/quota-orch 8080:8080 &
sleep 1
# from devbox:
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"o"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done
```
I can reproduce ~30% 500s when quota-orch delays >2.5s.

Ruth (support): customers asking for ETA and whether we can revert. Ticket is escalating (some have billing implications because they saw failed calls). @Marco (billing) flagged potential charge disputes.

Marco (billing): please tag me on final impact window. We need the list of customers affected and counts. If errors were returned as 5xx we treated calls as failed and some clients retried, inflating usage. Might cause double billing.

Amit (oncall): immediate mitigation suggestions:
- temporarily increase classifier timeout to 6s so quota-orch slow calls return 429 mapping if state indicates over-quota (if available)
- fallback: if classifier times out, the gateway should map to 429 if quota headers indicate over-limit, otherwise 503.
- add a short circuit on the edge: if x-quota-usage > x-quota-limit then return 429 without classifier call.

Claire (sre): I can flip a rule in the gateway policy to prefer 429 when x-quota-* headers are present. Doing a controlled toggle now in non-prod, then prod if good. Rolling out to 10% first.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by Claire: rollout/quota-classifier-fallback v2024.10.20-rc1 -> canary 10%

Evan (runtime): patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inc/edge/pull/4123 — added explicit mapping: classifier-timeout -> 429 if x-quota-usage >= x-quota-limit, else 503. Also added metrics so we can count timeout->429 conversions.

Amit (oncall): while canary is running, I'm going to raise quota-orch pod replica count and check connection pool settings. Scaling quota-orch +1 now.

Claire (sre): canary looks OK for 10m, error rates dropped from 12% to 1.2% for the test traffic simulating quota-exceed. Promoting to 50% now.

Ruth (support): customers updated: we told them we discovered a timeout-to-5xx mapping bug and we have a fix deploying. They're asking for reruns and whether calls will be retried. Suggest we proactively re-process any ingestions that failed due to 500 in the window?

Marco (billing): hold on reruns until we verify the mapping change. If we reprocess and clients were billed incorrectly we need to reconcile. I'll prepare a report for customers in the affected window (14:00Z–14:20Z).

Evan (runtime): note on root cause: quota-orch latency spike caused classifier to hit internal deadline. Edge code assumed classifier non-response = infrastructure error (5xx). It should check for quota state first. Adding unit tests for header-driven mapping.

Amit (oncall): timeline so far:
- 14:03Z spike begins (quota-orch slow)
- 14:05Z first support tickets
- 14:07Z oncall alerted
- 14:12Z gate fallback canary deployed (10%)
- 14:20Z promotion to 50%
- 14:28Z promotion to 100% and incident declared resolved for customer-facing 5xxs

Claire (sre): follow-ups for postmortem:
- add circuit-breaker and more aggressive autoscaling for quota-orch
- change default mapping semantics: classifier-timeout -> prefer 4xx if quota headers indicate limit exceeded
- improve observability: tag original classifier response code in gateway logs so support can see intended mapping
- add chaos test: simulate quota-orch 2-5s latency and ensure mapping behavior remains correct

Ruth (support): I'll send a customer-facing note and update tickets: root cause, mitigation, ETA for reconciles.

Marco (billing): request: provide list of request-ids and customer ids returned 500 in window. I will prepare credits if necessary.

Evan (runtime): PR merged and deployed to prod at 14:27Z. All green in metrics. Leaving incident open for postmortem write-up.

Amit (oncall): closing actions assigned:
- Evan: backport mapping change to edge-stable branch and add unit test (due EOD)
- Claire: implement autoscale policy + chaos test (due next sprint)
- Marco: impact report and customer credits proposal (due tomorrow)
- Ruth: customer comms draft + ticket updates (ASAP)

Ruth (support): thanks team. I'll escalate to customer success for sensitive customers. :thumbsup:

Evan (runtime): adding a short note for the postmortem draft: classifier and quota-orch should carry an idempotency/keyed-state header so edge can short-circuit on heavy-known-overquota signals rather than rely on classifier availability.

Claire (sre): marking incident P2 and assigning to eng-runtime and infra for the followups.

Ruth (support): final status update for tickets sent at 16:05Z. Customers acknowledged. Closing thread once postmortem posted.

(incident bot): incident 2024-10-20-quotamapper-5xx created, severity=P2, owner=Amit (oncall)
